content.content: A discard is admitted only in the trunk working copy. When a discard is invoked in a working copy other than the trunk working copy — the working copy whose root holds the store root — the deccy CLI shall refuse the invocation before it discards any draft, naming the workspace the invocation ran in, and shall discard nothing; a discard invoked in the trunk working copy proceeds. The admission and the refusal that enforces it are this decision's own addition: the rule that confines invocations writing graph state to the trunk, and the requirement sentence that restates it, are defined by writes to graph state and keep `draft` and `drafts` outside that set, so neither admits nor refuses a discard — a discard writes no node and no change. The working copy the sentence turns on is the one whose root holds the store root, a place rather than a change id or a workspace name, and the check it requires is on the working copy the invocation runs in, not on the workspace of the draft the invocation names. The refusal's wording, stream and exit status, the mechanism by which the invocation establishes which working copy it runs in, and the place of the check relative to the argument surface beyond "before it discards any draft" are not fixed here.
content.rationale:
This node records the commitment as a requirement sentence because the commitment is one admission rule on the CLI — when a discard is refused — and that is an obligation stated in words, at the same shape as the requirement sentence the trunk rule carries (mrwtusss). Every prerequisite is prose or a requirement in prose, so the rule is read off the recorded text rather than probed; there is nothing to run.

The rule is this node's own addition, and the text says so because the nearest prerequisites do not grant it. swuvzpvr fixes the trunk for every invocation that writes graph state and defines that set by the write, explicitly keeping `draft` and `drafts` outside it — one writes only a registry record, the other writes no graph state at all; mrwtusss restates the same set and the same exclusion in one requirement sentence. A discard writes no graph state: it creates no node and no change, records no edit into a node, and is not one of the three operations (tvxspkyy). So the trunk rule's set does not reach it and neither does the requirement sentence's restatement — and exclusion is not admission. Nothing in either node says where a discard may run, and this node does not read the confinement out of them: it states the admission, and the refusal outside the trunk, as its own addition, naming those two prerequisites only to say what they leave undecided.

The trunk the sentence turns on is lotlstzr's, taken as it stands and not narrowed: the store is rooted at the trunk and opened on the trunk root from any working copy, the trunk is the working copy whose root holds the state directory, and which working copy the invocation runs in does not move the store. Two consequences are why the rule can be stated as admission at all. The boundary is a place, so renaming the trunk or checking out a different change there does not move it, and no change id or workspace name makes an invocation trunk-side. And resolving that place from a draft working copy succeeds — the draft is a working copy of the same tree, and its repository entry names the trunk working copy — so a discard run there is refused as a matter of admission, not because the trunk could not be found. lotlstzr's own refusal for an unresolvable trunk is untouched, and this node adds no second root, no probe and no fallback; the requirement changes neither where the store is opened nor what a draft invocation opens.

What the refusal forbids is tvxspkyy's act: the end of an open draft that does not land, outside the operation vocabulary, writing no node and no change. Because that end is the whole of the act, `shall discard nothing` is not a list of effects but the single negative of the act — the draft stays open, with no landing behind it and no end. The two things a discard does reach are vxltqruo's and vzposmvm's: the abandonment of the working-copy change the draft's workspace holds, and the forget of that jj workspace with the removal of the directory the handle derives. The sentence covers both by placing the refusal before the discard begins, without restating either, fixing either's invocation or flags, or adding a step of its own.

The invocation the sentence constrains is kxyznwxu's: `deccy discard <handle>...`, one open draft per handle, answered whole — an invocation is one verb with its arguments, so it is either answered with the discards it names or refused, never half way. The sentence keeps that shape: the refusal is the invocation's, nothing it names is discarded, and the subject set is untouched because the check is on the working copy the invocation runs in and not on the workspace of the draft it names. Drift therefore still does not shrink the subject set, no existence test on a draft's workspace is added, and the argument surface and its ordering ahead of the store stay exactly where kxyznwxu puts them.

mrwtusss carries the sentence's form rather than its content: one obligation with the trigger first, the response second, the naming of the workspace the invocation ran in, and the exclusions and deferrals after the semicolon. This node follows that form for a different subject and takes the naming as the form states it — the caller's own working copy, so the caller can tell which workspace was refused. The deferrals it repeats are the same in kind, and no property mrwtusss fixes for its own refusal is narrowed or decided a second time.

Deliberately not settled, because each can change without moving the rule: the refusal's wording, stream and exit status; the mechanism by which the invocation establishes which working copy it runs in; the place of the check relative to the argument surface beyond `before it discards any draft`; and what becomes of the record, of the change and of the workspace, which are the store's removal, vxltqruo's and vzposmvm's, relied on here rather than restated.
